title: SHINIGAMAE
subtitle: Personal digital workshop
problem: Everything I make lived in five different places, none of which I owned, and none of which talked to each other.
approach: Design the language first in Figma, then build a static Astro shell against it, with a token layer strict enough that the design cannot drift silently. Five sync scripts pull the sources in and commit what they find, so no page waits on someone else's API to render.
result: This site — 479 pages off five feeds, a dark ground and a light one, and a drift report that says when code and design have stopped agreeing.
lessons: Publishing styles in Figma matters more than any sync script
A token layer is only real if nothing can bypass it — a second theme then costs one file
A feed you sync and commit beats an API you call at read time
Deciding the shell before the pages saved a rewrite

title: BUILD LOG PIPELINE
subtitle: Photo ingest for the model archive
problem: Build photos sat on a phone in no particular order, and writing them up by hand meant they never got written up.
approach: A small ingest step that reads EXIF, groups shots by session, and drafts an entry skeleton to edit rather than author from scratch.
result: Drafting a build entry went from an evening to a few minutes.
lessons: The bottleneck was writing, not storage
Generating a draft to edit beats generating a finished thing

title: READING TIMELINE
subtitle: Goodreads without the noise
problem: I wanted the shape of a reading year, not a feed of other people's reviews.
approach: Pull my own shelf data, reduce it to finish dates and a single personal note per book, and render it as one line.
result: A year of reading readable at a glance.
lessons: One sentence per book is more honest than a star rating
Most of the data was not worth keeping
